**Observations from the image:**

- **Plant type**: Brassica (cabbage/kale type leaf, identifiable by shape and surface texture)
- **Affected part**: Leaf — showing both upper and lower surfaces
- **Color**: Large irregular yellow-green chlorotic patches transitioning to tan/brown necrosis
- **Texture/pattern**: Areas of whitish-gray coating visible on the leaf surface — consistent with fungal sporulation; lesions appear somewhat bounded by leaf veins (angular)
- **Overall appearance**: Leaf partially collapsed/wilted in affected zones; no obvious concentric ring patterns (rules out Alternaria), no V-shaped lesions from margins (rules out Black Rot), no slimy tissue breakdown (rules out Bacterial Soft Rot)

**Reasoning through the classes:**

| Class | Key Diagnostic | Match? |
|---|---|---|
| Alternaria Leaf Spot | Dark circular spots with concentric rings/target pattern | No — no concentric rings |
| Bacterial Soft Rot | Water-soaked, slimy, mushy tissue collapse | No — no sliminess |
| Black Rot | V-shaped chlorosis from leaf margins, dark veins | No — no V-shaped lesion |
| Downy Mildew | Yellow patches on upper surface, grayish-white downy growth (sporulation) on underside, angular lesions | **Yes** — matches chlorotic patches, whitish-gray coating, angular lesion boundaries on a brassica host |

The whitish-gray sporulation layer combined with angular yellow chlorotic patches on a brassica leaf is the hallmark signature of **Downy Mildew** (*Peronospora parasitica* on brassicas).
